nodes.label: Capabilio Frontend Architecture Restructuring Plan
nodes.rationale: The stack is React+Vite SPA, not Next.js (no App Router/SSR/file-based routing); recommends staying on Vite + React Router v6 rather than migrating to Next.js, though the feature-folder structure would map directly to App Router route groups later with zero business-logic rework.

nodes.label: Feature-Folder Structure (features/<path>/<page>/)
nodes.rationale: Every page owns exactly PageName.jsx + tabs.config.js + components/ + hooks/ + index.js; domain logic is path-isolated (features/student/, features/professional/, etc.) so student and organization logic never cross-import.

nodes.label: Config-Driven Navigation and Tabs
nodes.rationale: Nav arrays live in config/nav/*.nav.js and tab arrays in config/tabs/<path>/<page>.tabs.js so navigation is never hardcoded in components (replaces PATH_META/STUDENT_HEADER_NAV baked into the old App.jsx).

nodes.label: Permission Model (ROLE_PATHS / PAGE_ROLES / PathGuard)
nodes.rationale: ROLE_PATHS maps profile path/org_type to accessible URL prefixes, checked by PathGuard at the route level so URL-bar access to the wrong path redirects to the user's real home.

nodes.label: 12-Phase Migration Plan
nodes.rationale: Sequenced so each phase is independently deployable and nothing breaks between steps: cleanup -> install React Router -> scaffold folders -> extract providers -> extract auth UI -> move pages path-by-path -> move components -> shared UI cleanup -> config system -> services/store -> aliases -> delete old pages/ -> consolidate styles.

nodes.label: Anti-Mess Rules
nodes.rationale: Explicit team/PR checklist of prohibitions: no mixed-path pages/, App.jsx never exceeds ~30 lines, no hardcoded nav/tab arrays, no currentPage string-state routing, no .bak files committed, no direct fetch() outside services/*.service.js, no page file over 400 lines.
